heart.name: Heart (Cor)
heart.description: A muscular organ roughly the size of a closed fist that pumps blood throughout the circulatory system via rhythmic contractions.
heart.location: Middle mediastinum of the thorax, between the lungs, posterior to the sternum, tilted leftward.
heart.function: Drives systemic and pulmonary circulation. Right atrium and ventricle handle deoxygenated blood to the lungs; left atrium and ventricle pump oxygenated blood to the body.
heart.clinical_notes: Prone to coronary artery disease, myocardial infarction, arrhythmias, and valvular stenosis.

brain.name: Brain (Encephalon)
brain.description: The central information-processing organ of the nervous system, enclosed within the cranium.
brain.location: Cranial cavity of the skull, superior to the brainstem and spinal cord.
brain.function: Controls cognitive function, sensory processing, motor control, memory, emotion, and homeostatic regulation.
brain.clinical_notes: Susceptible to ischemic stroke, hemorrhagic stroke, traumatic brain injury, and neurodegenerative disorders such as Alzheimer's.

cerebellum.name: Cerebellum
cerebellum.description: Known as the 'little brain', situated beneath the occipital lobes.
cerebellum.location: Posterior cranial fossa, posterior to the pons and medulla oblongata.
cerebellum.function: Coordinates voluntary muscular movements, maintains posture, balance, and motor learning.
cerebellum.clinical_notes: Lesions lead to ataxia, intention tremor, dysmetria, and nystagmus.

brainstem.name: Brainstem
brainstem.description: Comprises the midbrain, pons, and medulla oblongata connecting the cerebrum to the spinal cord.
brainstem.location: Base of the brain, passing through the foramen magnum.
brainstem.function: Controls autonomic vital reflexes including respiration, heart rate, blood pressure, and swallowing.
brainstem.clinical_notes: Brainstem stroke or herniation can cause locked-in syndrome or rapid respiratory arrest.

lungs.name: Lungs (Pulmones)
lungs.description: Paired cone-shaped organs of respiration where gas exchange takes place.
lungs.location: Thoracic cavity on either side of the mediastinum, protected by the ribcage.
lungs.function: Exchanges oxygen from inhaled air with carbon dioxide from pulmonary capillary blood.
lungs.clinical_notes: Vulnerable to pneumonia, asthma, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), and pneumothorax.

trachea.name: Trachea (Windpipe)
trachea.description: A cartilaginous tube reinforced by C-shaped hyaline cartilage rings.
trachea.location: Mediastinum, descending from the cricoid cartilage (C6) to the carina (T4/T5).
trachea.function: Conducts air from the larynx to the primary bronchi; mucociliary clearance traps inhaled pathogens.
trachea.clinical_notes: May require tracheostomy in cases of upper airway obstruction.

liver.name: Liver (Hepar)
liver.description: The largest internal solid organ and primary metabolic powerhouse of the human body.
liver.location: Right hypochondriac and epigastric regions of the abdominal cavity, inferior to the diaphragm.
liver.function: Bile synthesis, glycogen storage, protein synthesis (albumin, clotting factors), and chemical detoxification.
liver.clinical_notes: Prone to cirrhosis, non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD), hepatitis, and portal hypertension.

stomach.name: Stomach (Gaster)
stomach.description: A J-shaped distensible muscular reservoir of the gastrointestinal tract.
stomach.location: Left upper quadrant and epigastrium, between the esophagus and duodenum.
stomach.function: Mechanical churning and chemical digestion of food via gastric acid (HCl) and pepsinogen into chyme.
stomach.clinical_notes: Commonly afflicted by peptic ulcer disease, GERD, Helicobacter pylori infection, and gastritis.

spleen.name: Spleen (Lien)
spleen.description: A purplish secondary lymphoid organ containing red pulp and white pulp.
spleen.location: Left hypochondrium, posterior to the stomach and anterior to ribs 9-11.
spleen.function: Filters blood, recycles old erythrocytes, stores platelets, and mounts immune responses against blood-borne antigens.
spleen.clinical_notes: Subject to rupture in blunt abdominal trauma; splenomegaly occurs in mononucleosis and malaria.

pancreas.name: Pancreas
pancreas.description: An elongated retroperitoneal heterocrine gland with head, uncinate process, body, and tail.
pancreas.location: Posterior to the stomach, extending transversely from the C-loop of the duodenum to the splenic hilum.
pancreas.function: Endocrine: secretes insulin and glucagon. Exocrine: secretes digestive enzymes (amylase, lipase, trypsin).
pancreas.clinical_notes: Pancreatitis, type 1 and type 2 diabetes mellitus, and adenocarcinoma of the pancreatic head.

kidneys.name: Kidneys (Renes)
kidneys.description: Pair of bean-shaped retroperitoneal organs with renal cortex, medulla, and nephrons.
kidneys.location: Posterior abdominal wall between T12 and L3; the right kidney is slightly lower due to the liver.
kidneys.function: Filtration of metabolic waste (urea, creatinine), regulation of electrolyte balance, fluid volume, and renin secretion.
kidneys.clinical_notes: Nephrolithiasis (kidney stones), acute kidney injury, chronic kidney disease, and glomerulonephritis.

small_intestine.name: Small Intestine
small_intestine.description: Divided into duodenum, jejunum, and ileum with high mucosal surface area from circular folds and villi.
small_intestine.location: Central and lower abdominal cavity, framed by the large intestine.
small_intestine.function: Primary site of nutrient digestion and absorption (carbohydrates, amino acids, lipids, vitamins).
small_intestine.clinical_notes: Celiac disease, Crohn's disease, and mechanical small bowel obstruction.

large_intestine.name: Large Intestine (Colon)
large_intestine.description: Consists of cecum, ascending colon, transverse colon, descending colon, sigmoid colon, and rectum.
large_intestine.location: Periphery of the abdominal cavity, framing the small intestine.
large_intestine.function: Absorption of water and electrolytes, fermentation of indigestible fiber by gut microbiota, feces formation.
large_intestine.clinical_notes: Ulcerative colitis, colorectal carcinoma, diverticulitis, and acute appendicitis.

bladder.name: Urinary Bladder (Vesica Urinaria)
bladder.description: A hollow distensible muscular organ with a detrusor muscle wall and trigone.
bladder.location: Lesser pelvis, resting on the pelvic floor posterior to the pubic symphysis.
bladder.function: Stores up to 400-600 mL of urine before micturition via coordinated detrusor contraction and sphincter relaxation.
bladder.clinical_notes: Urinary tract infections (cystitis), urinary incontinence, and transitional cell carcinoma.

uterus.name: Uterus (Womb)
uterus.description: A hollow, thick-walled muscular organ shaped like an inverted pear, consisting of fundus, body, and cervix.
uterus.location: Female pelvic cavity between the urinary bladder anteriorly and the rectum posteriorly.
uterus.function: Houses and nourishes the developing embryo and fetus throughout gestation; undergoes cyclic endometrial shedding during menstruation.
uterus.clinical_notes: Uterine leiomyomas (fibroids), endometriosis, cervical dysplasia (HPV-related), and adenomyosis.

fallopian_tubes.name: Fallopian Tubes (Uterine Tubes)
fallopian_tubes.description: Bilateral muscular canals extending from the uterine horns toward the ovaries, lined with ciliated epithelium.
fallopian_tubes.location: Within the superior margin of the broad ligament in the female pelvic cavity.
fallopian_tubes.function: Transports the ovum from the ovary toward the uterus; typical anatomical site of fertilization (ampulla).
fallopian_tubes.clinical_notes: Ectopic tubal pregnancy, pelvic inflammatory disease (PID), and salpingitis causing tubal occlusion.

ovaries.name: Ovaries
ovaries.description: Paired almond-shaped female gonads situated in the ovarian fossa of the lateral pelvic wall.
ovaries.location: Posterior aspect of the broad ligament, attached via the ovarian ligament and mesovarium.
ovaries.function: Oogenesis (production of mature ova) and endocrine synthesis of estrogen and progesterone.
ovaries.clinical_notes: Polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS), ovarian torsion, and epithelial ovarian malignancies.

mammary_glands.name: Breasts (Mammary Glands)
mammary_glands.description: Modified apocrine sweat glands composed of glandular lobules, lactiferous ducts, and adipose tissue.
mammary_glands.location: Anterior thoracic wall overlying the pectoralis major muscles from ribs 2 to 6.
mammary_glands.function: Lactation and milk secretion driven by prolactin and oxytocin during the postpartum period.
mammary_glands.clinical_notes: Invasive ductal carcinoma, fibroadenoma, mastitis during breastfeeding, and BRCA1/2 genetic mutations.

penis.name: Penis
penis.description: The male external copulatory and urinary organ composed of three erectile cylinders: two corpora cavernosa and one corpus spongiosum.
penis.location: Anterior perineum, suspended from the front and sides of the pubic arch.
penis.function: Urination via the penile urethra and semen delivery during sexual intercourse via erectile tumescence.
penis.clinical_notes: Erectile dysfunction, phimosis, priapism, and Peyronie's disease.

testes.name: Testes & Scrotum
testes.description: The male primary gonads suspended within the cutaneous scrotal sac.
testes.location: Posteroinferior to the penis, outside the abdominopelvic cavity for thermoregulation.
testes.function: Spermatogenesis inside seminiferous tubules and endocrine secretion of testosterone by Leydig cells.
testes.clinical_notes: Testicular torsion (surgical emergency), cryptorchidism, varicocele, and seminoma.

prostate.name: Prostate Gland
prostate.description: A walnut-sized fibromuscular gland surrounding the prostatic urethra.
prostate.location: Pelvic cavity, directly inferior to the bladder neck and anterior to the rectum.
prostate.function: Produces an alkaline prostatic fluid that constitutes approximately 30% of semen volume, nourishing sperm.
prostate.clinical_notes: Benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH) causing urinary retention, prostatitis, and prostate adenocarcinoma.

pectoralis_major.name: Pectoralis Major Muscle
pectoralis_major.description: A thick, fan-shaped muscle covering the upper anterior chest wall.
pectoralis_major.location: Origin: medial half of clavicle, sternum, and costal cartilages 1-6. Insertion: lateral lip of the bicipital groove of humerus.
pectoralis_major.function: Adduction, medial rotation, and horizontal flexion of the arm at the glenohumeral joint.
pectoralis_major.clinical_notes: Tears can occur during heavy bench-press movements; absence seen in congenital Poland syndrome.

rectus_abdominis.name: Rectus Abdominis Muscle
rectus_abdominis.description: Long paired strap muscle forming the anterior abdominal wall ('abs'), separated into distinct segments by tendinous intersections.
rectus_abdominis.location: Origin: pubic crest and pubic symphysis. Insertion: xiphoid process and costal cartilages 5-7.
rectus_abdominis.function: Flexion of the lumbar spine, stabilization of the pelvis, and compression of abdominal viscera during forced expiration.
rectus_abdominis.clinical_notes: Prone to rectus sheath hematoma and diastasis recti (separation along linea alba, often postpartum).

linea_alba.name: Linea Alba & Tendinous Sheath
linea_alba.description: A tough fibrous band running down the midline of the abdomen formed by the bilateral aponeuroses of the abdominal muscles.
linea_alba.location: Midline of anterior abdominal wall from xiphoid process to pubic symphysis.
linea_alba.function: Binds the rectus abdominis muscles and stabilizes anterior abdominal pressure.
linea_alba.clinical_notes: Frequent site for surgical incisions (laparotomy) and epigastric/umbilical hernias.

external_oblique.name: External Oblique Muscle
external_oblique.description: The largest and most superficial of the three lateral abdominal muscles, with fibers directed inferomedially.
external_oblique.location: Origin: external surfaces of ribs 5-12. Insertion: linea alba, pubic tubercle, and anterior half of iliac crest.
external_oblique.function: Contralateral rotation of the torso, lateral flexion of the vertebral column, and compression of abdominal contents.
external_oblique.clinical_notes: Its lower aponeurotic border forms the inguinal ligament, critical in inguinal hernia evaluations.

serratus_anterior.name: Serratus Anterior Muscle
serratus_anterior.description: A saw-toothed muscle originating from the upper eight ribs and wrapping around the thoracic wall to the medial scapular border.
serratus_anterior.location: Lateral thoracic wall beneath the armpit and pectoral muscles.
serratus_anterior.function: Protracts and stabilizes the scapula against the thoracic wall; upwardly rotates the glenoid cavity.
serratus_anterior.clinical_notes: Injury to the long thoracic nerve (C5-C7) results in medial scapular winging ('winged scapula').

deltoid.name: Deltoid Muscle
deltoid.description: A triangular muscle capping the shoulder joint with anterior (clavicular), lateral (acromial), and posterior (spinal) heads.
deltoid.location: Origin: lateral third of clavicle, acromion, and spine of scapula. Insertion: deltoid tuberosity of humerus.
deltoid.function: Abduction of the arm from 15 to 90 degrees (lateral fibers); flexion and medial rotation (anterior); extension (posterior).
deltoid.clinical_notes: Primary clinical site for intramuscular vaccine injections; innervated by the axillary nerve.

biceps_brachii.name: Biceps Brachii Muscle
biceps_brachii.description: A prominent two-headed muscle on the anterior compartment of the arm.
biceps_brachii.location: Origin: short head from coracoid process, long head from supraglenoid tubercle. Insertion: radial tuberosity and bicipital aponeurosis.
biceps_brachii.function: Powerful supinator of the flexed forearm and secondary flexor of the elbow joint.
biceps_brachii.clinical_notes: Rupture of the long head tendon causes the classic 'Popeye deformity' of the anterior arm.

triceps_brachii.name: Triceps Brachii Muscle
triceps_brachii.description: A large three-headed muscle on the posterior compartment of the arm.
triceps_brachii.location: Origin: long head from infraglenoid tubercle, lateral and medial heads from humerus. Insertion: olecranon of ulna.
triceps_brachii.function: Chief extensor of the elbow joint; long head assists with arm extension and adduction.
triceps_brachii.clinical_notes: Innervated by the radial nerve; radial nerve palsy (e.g. spiral groove fracture) causes wrist drop.

brachioradialis.name: Brachioradialis Muscle
brachioradialis.description: Superficial forearm muscle running along the radial side, forming the lateral boundary of the cubital fossa.
brachioradialis.location: Origin: upper two-thirds of lateral supracondylar ridge of humerus. Insertion: styloid process of radius.
brachioradialis.function: Flexes the elbow joint when the forearm is in a semi-pronated ('handshake') position.
brachioradialis.clinical_notes: Tested in neurological examinations via the brachioradialis deep tendon reflex (C5/C6).

rectus_femoris.name: Rectus Femoris (Quadriceps)
rectus_femoris.description: The central anterior superficial belly of the quadriceps femoris, crossing both the hip and knee joints.
rectus_femoris.location: Origin: anterior inferior iliac spine (AIIS). Insertion: patella and tibial tuberosity via the patellar tendon.
rectus_femoris.function: Extends the leg at the knee joint and assists in flexing the thigh at the hip joint.
rectus_femoris.clinical_notes: Frequently strained or avulsed in sprinters and soccer kickers.

vastus_lateralis.name: Vastus Lateralis Muscle
vastus_lateralis.description: The largest and most lateral head of the quadriceps femoris muscle.
vastus_lateralis.location: Origin: greater trochanter and lateral lip of linea aspera of femur. Insertion: lateral border of patella.
vastus_lateralis.function: Powerful extension of the leg at the knee joint.
vastus_lateralis.clinical_notes: Common site for pediatric intramuscular injections.

vastus_medialis.name: Vastus Medialis Muscle (VMO)
vastus_medialis.description: Teardrop-shaped medial head of the quadriceps muscle directly superior to the medial patellar margin.
vastus_medialis.location: Origin: medial lip of linea aspera and intertrochanteric line. Insertion: medial border of patella.
vastus_medialis.function: Extends the knee and tracks the patella medially to counteract lateral subluxation forces.
vastus_medialis.clinical_notes: VMO weakness is strongly implicated in patellofemoral pain syndrome.

sartorius.name: Sartorius Muscle ('Tailor's Muscle')
sartorius.description: The longest muscle in the human body, crossing the anterior thigh diagonally.
sartorius.location: Origin: anterior superior iliac spine (ASIS). Insertion: medial surface of proximal tibia (pes anserinus).
sartorius.function: Flexes, abducts, and laterally rotates the thigh at the hip; flexes the knee (cross-legged sitting position).
sartorius.clinical_notes: Its insertion forms the pes anserinus with gracilis and semitendinosus; subject to pes anserine bursitis.

patellar_tendon.name: Patellar Tendon (Ligament)
patellar_tendon.description: A dense, fibrous band continuing from the apex of the patella to the tibial tuberosity.
patellar_tendon.location: Anterior aspect of the knee joint.
patellar_tendon.function: Transmits the powerful tensile force of the quadriceps femoris to the tibia for knee extension.
patellar_tendon.clinical_notes: Tapped during the L3/L4 patellar tendon reflex; subject to jumper's knee (patellar tendinopathy) and Osgood-Schlatter disease.

tibialis_anterior.name: Tibialis Anterior Muscle
tibialis_anterior.description: The most prominent muscle of the anterior compartment of the lower leg.
tibialis_anterior.location: Origin: lateral condyle and upper half of lateral surface of tibia. Insertion: medial cuneiform and base of 1st metatarsal.
tibialis_anterior.function: Dorsiflexion of the ankle and inversion of the foot at subtalar joints; supports the medial longitudinal arch.
tibialis_anterior.clinical_notes: Paralysis caused by deep fibular (peroneal) nerve injury leads to steppage gait ('foot drop').

gastrocnemius.name: Gastrocnemius Muscle (Calf)
gastrocnemius.description: Superficial two-headed muscle creating the rounded contour of the calf.
gastrocnemius.location: Origin: lateral and medial condyles of the femur. Insertion: posterior calcaneus via the Achilles tendon.
gastrocnemius.function: Plantarflexion of the foot at the ankle joint and flexion of the leg at the knee joint.
gastrocnemius.clinical_notes: Frequently affected by calf muscle strains and nocturnal muscle cramps.

achilles_tendon.name: Achilles Tendon (Calcaneal Tendon)
achilles_tendon.description: The thickest and strongest tendon in the human body, joining the gastrocnemius and soleus to the calcaneus.
achilles_tendon.function: Transmits plantarflexion forces essential for walking, running, and jumping.
achilles_tendon.clinical_notes: Achilles tendon rupture occurs typically 2-6 cm above the calcaneal insertion; evaluated via the Thompson test.

aorta.name: Aorta & Aortic Arch
aorta.description: The main artery of the body, carrying oxygen-rich blood from the left ventricle into systemic circulation.
aorta.location: Emerges from the aortic root, arches superiorly over the pulmonary trunk (T4 level), and descends through thorax and abdomen.
aorta.function: Distributes high-pressure oxygenated arterial blood to all tissues; its elastic recoil smooths diastolic pressure.
aorta.clinical_notes: Aortic dissection (Stanford types A and B), abdominal aortic aneurysm (AAA), and coarctation of the aorta.

carotid_artery.name: Carotid Arteries
carotid_artery.description: Major bilateral arteries supplying oxygenated blood to the head, face, and brain.
carotid_artery.location: Carotid sheath of the anterior triangle of the neck, bifurcating at C4 into internal and external carotid arteries.
carotid_artery.function: Internal carotid supplies the Circle of Willis and cerebrum; external carotid supplies face, scalp, and neck.
carotid_artery.clinical_notes: Carotid atherosclerosis leads to transient ischemic attacks (TIAs) and strokes; evaluated via carotid duplex ultrasound.

femoral_vessels.name: Femoral Vessels (Artery & Vein)
femoral_vessels.description: The chief arterial and venous conduits of the lower extremity.
femoral_vessels.location: Femoral triangle of the anterior proximal thigh beneath the inguinal ligament (lateral to medial: NAVEL).
femoral_vessels.function: Supplies arterial blood to the lower limb (femoral artery) and returns venous blood to external iliac veins (femoral vein).
femoral_vessels.clinical_notes: Standard anatomical site for cardiac catheterization, arterial blood gas sampling, and deep vein thrombosis (DVT).

vena_cava.name: Superior & Inferior Vena Cava
vena_cava.description: The two largest systemic veins delivering deoxygenated blood back to the right atrium of the heart.
vena_cava.location: SVC: right anterolateral superior mediastinum. IVC: retroperitoneum along the right anterolateral aspect of the spine.
vena_cava.function: SVC drains the head, neck, upper limbs, and thorax; IVC drains the abdomen, pelvis, and lower limbs.
vena_cava.clinical_notes: SVC syndrome (often from mediastinal bronchogenic carcinoma) and IVC filters placed for pulmonary embolism prevention.

jugular_vein.name: Internal Jugular Vein
jugular_vein.description: Major paired deep vein collecting venous blood from the brain, superficial parts of the face, and neck.
jugular_vein.location: Carotid sheath of the neck, lateral to the internal carotid artery and vagus nerve.
jugular_vein.function: Drains the cranial dural venous sinuses into the brachiocephalic vein.
jugular_vein.clinical_notes: Common site for central venous catheter (CVC) placement; jugular venous pressure (JVP) assesses right atrial filling pressure.

cranium.name: Cranium (Skull)
cranium.description: The skeletal framework of the head composed of the neurocranium (braincase) and viscerocranium (facial skeleton).
cranium.location: Superior terminus of the vertebral column.
cranium.function: Protects the brain and special sensory organs (eyes, inner ear); anchors facial musculature.
cranium.clinical_notes: Skull fractures (basilar skull fracture with Battle sign or raccoon eyes), craniosynostosis in infants.

mandible.name: Mandible (Lower Jaw)
mandible.description: The largest, strongest, and only movable bone of the facial skeleton.
mandible.location: Inferior portion of the facial skeleton, articulating with the temporal bones at the temporomandibular joints (TMJ).
mandible.function: Houses the lower dental arch and provides insertion for muscles of mastication (masseter, temporalis, pterygoids).
mandible.clinical_notes: TMJ dysfunction syndrome and mandibular fractures frequently occurring at the condylar neck or angle.

vertebrae.name: Vertebral Column (Spine)
vertebrae.description: Series of 33 vertebrae (7 cervical, 12 thoracic, 5 lumbar, 5 fused sacral, 4 fused coccygeal) separated by fibrocartilaginous discs.
vertebrae.location: Dorsal midline of the trunk from the base of the cranium to the coccyx.
vertebrae.function: Houses and protects the spinal cord, supports the weight of the head and torso, and permits multidirectional flexibility.
vertebrae.clinical_notes: Herniated intervertebral disc (sciatica), scoliosis, spinal stenosis, and osteoporosis-induced vertebral compression fractures.

ribcage.name: Ribcage (Thoracic Cage)
ribcage.description: Osteocartilaginous cage formed by 12 pairs of ribs, costal cartilages, thoracic vertebrae, and the sternum.
ribcage.function: Encloses and protects vital cardiopulmonary organs; expands during inspiration via intercostal muscle action.
ribcage.clinical_notes: Rib fractures, flail chest (paradoxical respiration from multiple segmental fractures), and costochondritis.

sternum.name: Sternum (Breastbone)
sternum.description: Flat, elongated T-shaped bone situated at the anterior thoracic midline, divided into manubrium, body, and xiphoid process.
sternum.location: Anterior midline of the chest wall.
sternum.function: Anchors the anterior ends of the true ribs via costal cartilages and clavicles via sternoclavicular joints.
sternum.clinical_notes: Median sternotomy for open-heart cardiac procedures; site for bone marrow aspirates.

pelvis.name: Pelvic Girdle (Pelvis)
pelvis.description: Ring of bones consisting of the paired hip bones (ilium, ischium, pubis) and the posterior sacrum and coccyx.
pelvis.location: Base of the spine, linking the trunk to the lower extremities.
pelvis.function: Transfers upper body weight to the femurs; houses and shelters pelvic viscera (bladder, rectum, reproductive organs).
pelvis.clinical_notes: High-energy pelvic ring fractures can cause life-threatening retroperitoneal hemorrhage; sexual dimorphism in gynecoid vs. android pelvis.

femur.name: Femur (Thigh Bone)
femur.description: The longest, heaviest, and strongest long bone in the human skeleton.
femur.location: Thigh, between the hip joint (acetabulum) and knee joint.
femur.function: Supports the body's total mass during bipedal locomotion; serves as attachment for powerful hip and knee muscles.
femur.clinical_notes: Femoral neck fractures are prevalent in osteoporotic elderly individuals, often requiring arthroplasty due to avascular necrosis risk.

patella.name: Patella (Kneecap)
patella.description: The largest sesamoid bone in the human body, embedded inside the quadriceps tendon.
patella.location: Anterior surface of the knee joint.
patella.function: Increases the mechanical lever arm of the quadriceps tendon, improving knee extension efficiency.
patella.clinical_notes: Patellar dislocation (usually lateral), patellar fractures, and chondromalacia patellae.

tibia.name: Tibia & Fibula (Shin & Calf Bones)
tibia.description: The paired bones of the leg: the tibia is the medial, weight-bearing bone; the fibula is the slender lateral stabilizing bone.
tibia.location: Lower leg between the knee and ankle joints.
tibia.function: Tibia transmits body weight from the femur to the talus; fibula provides muscle attachments and forms the lateral malleolus.
tibia.clinical_notes: Tibial shaft fractures are the most common long-bone fractures, often open due to its subcutaneous anterior border.

integumentary.name: Skin (Integumentary System)
integumentary.description: The largest organ of the human body, covering external surfaces with epidermis, dermis, and hypodermis.
integumentary.location: External anatomical boundary of the entire human body.
integumentary.function: Physical barrier protection against microorganisms, UV radiation, thermoregulation (sweat/vasodilation), and sensation.
integumentary.clinical_notes: Burn evaluations (Rule of Nines), melanoma, basal cell carcinoma, atopic dermatitis, and pressure ulcers.
